source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Predict whether a thin glass plate, convex lens, or concave lens will pass, converge, or diverge multiple parallel light beams.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: thin glass plate is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: The comparison is made with multiple parallel beams of light.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when The comparison is made with multiple parallel beams of light is not true.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Judge from the most visible feature in the figure, not from the mechanism's test.

intelligence.enrichment: A thin glass plate lets the light beam pass as it is, a convex lens converges the light falling on it, and a concave lens diverges the light falling on it. transparent optical element shape determines whether transmitted parallel beams pass unchanged, converge, or diverge The learner predicts whether a thin glass plate, convex lens, or concave lens passes, converges, or diverges multiple parallel beams. Any transparent object bends parallel light beams, so even a thin glass plate must converge or diverge the beams.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Light: mirrors and lenses. The student must decide: Predict whether a thin glass plate, convex lens, or concave lens will pass, converge, or diverge multiple parallel light beams. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
